==English== {{wp|+ity (mathematics)}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|æqual|æquall||obsolete}} ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:equal|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|equal}}, from {{der|en|la|aequālis}}. {{dbt|en|aequalis|egal}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈiːkwəl/}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈiːkəl/|a=dialectal,archaic|ref={{R:Hall PGSMS|3|2|88}}}} * {{audio|en|en-us-equal.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-equal.wav|a=GA}} * {{rhymes|en|iːkwəl|s=2}} ===Adjective=== {{en-adj|-,more}} # {{lb|en|not comparable}} The same in one or more respects. #: {{nearsyn|en|equivalent#Adjective|Thesaurus:equal}} #* {{RQ:en:New York Times |date=2025-08-30 |author=Katrina Miller |authorlink=Katrina Miller |title=You Don't Need to Be Good at Math to Enjoy It. In her latest book, Eugenia Cheng, a mathematician, explores the choices we make to determine if two things — numbers, shapes, words and even people — are '''equal'''. 'A Conversation With' column |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/30/science/eugenia-cheng-math-unequal-book.html |passage=Dr. [[w:Eugenia Cheng|[Eugenia] Cheng]]'s latest book, ''Unequal: The Math of When Things Do and Don’t Add Up,'' is all about equations and will be released in the United States on Tuesday. But it is more than a regurgitation of the many formulas you may recall learning in high school. In the book, Dr. Cheng argues that an equation — in its barest sense, a declaration that two things are '''equal''' — can be a profound statement on the choices we make about what is or is not the same. For example, 2 × 3 may equal 3 × 2. But two packs of three cookies each is distinct from three packs of two cookies each. A cube drawn face-on versus from one edge looks different, though we understand the two shapes to be the same. "Almost everything can be considered '''equal''' and unequal at the same time," Dr. Cheng wrote. "And it's up to us what we do about it."|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251225202114/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/30/science/eugenia-cheng-math-unequal-book.html|archivedate=25 December 2025}} ## {{lb|en|usually|not comparable}} The same in value (status, merit, etc): having or deserving the same [[right]]s or treatment. ##: {{ux|en|We hold that all men are created '''equal''' and are thus '''equal''' under the law.}} ##* {{RQ:Orwell Animal Farm|text=All animals are '''equal''', but some animals are more '''equal''' than the others.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1983|title=Law & Inequality |text=[Under] the combat exclusion [preventing women from serving in combat...] Women are not '''equal''' citizens; women are a certain kind of citizen, a separate class with distinctly lower status.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|author=Kari Melby|author2=Christina Carlsson Wetterberg|author3=Anna-Birte Ravn|title=Gender Equality and Welfare Politics in Scandinavia: The Limits of Political Ambition?|publisher=Policy Press|isbn=9781847424655|page=57 |text={{...}} women and men should be '''equal''' regarding civil rights / the right to occupational work.}} ## The same in all respects that matter practically; [[interchangeable]], [[fungible]], or (even sometimes) [[identical]] for practical purposes. ##: {{ux|en|'''Equal''' conditions should produce '''equal''' results.}} ##: {{ux|en|All else being '''equal''', we can expect this factor to have no discernible effect by itself.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1705|author={{w|George Cheyne (physician)|George Cheyne}}|title=The Philosophical Principles of Religion Natural and Revealed |passage=They who are not disposed to receive them may let them alone or reject them; it is '''equal''' to me.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1980|month=July |author=w:Frank Herbert|title=Dune Genesis|journal={{w|Omni (magazine)|Omni}} |url=https://archive.org/details/sim_omni_1980-07_2_10/ |volume=2|issue=10|issn=0149-8711|oclc=440821199|page=74 |pageurl=https://archive.org/details/sim_omni_1980-07_2_10/page/74/|column=2 |url2=https://web.archive.org/web/20211024130520/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5ga4PYMKwQ0 |title2=Ultimate Guide To Dune (Part 2) Book One|series2=1:11:30|year2=2017 |text=I now believe that evolution, or deevolution, never ends short of death, that no society has ever achieved an absolute pinnacle, that all humans are not created '''equal'''. In fact, I believe attempts to create some abstract equalization create a morass of injustices that rebound on the equalizers. '''Equal''' justice and '''equal''' opportunity are ideals we should seek, but we should recognize that humans administer the ideals and that humans do not have '''equal''' ability.}} ## {{lb|en|mathematics|not comparable}} Exactly identical, having the same [[value]]. ##: {{ux|en|All right angles are '''equal'''.}} ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=10|passage=The skipper Mr. Cooke had hired at Far Harbor was a God-fearing man with a luke warm interest in his new billet and employer, and had only been prevailed upon to take charge of the yacht after the offer of an emolument '''equal''' to half a year's sea pay of an ensign in the navy.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[fair|Fair]], [[impartial]]. #: {{syn|en|objective|unbiased|Thesaurus:impartial}} #* {{RQ:Milton Areopagitica| pretty tough, but I think I'm '''equal''' to it.}} #: {{coa|en|be '''equal''' to the task}} #* {{RQ:Melville Moby-Dick|chapter=X|passage=Here was a man some twenty thousand miles from home, by the way of Cape Horn, that is—which was the only way he could get there—thrown among people as strange to him as though he were in the planet Jupiter; and yet he seemed entirely at his ease; preserving the utmost serenity; content with his own companionship; always '''equal''' to himself.}} #* {{RQ:Austen Emma|text=her comprehension was certainly more '''equal''' to the covert meaning, the superior intelligence, of those five letters so arranged.}} #* {{RQ:Clarendon History|passage=The Scots trusted not their own numbers as '''equal''' to fight with the English.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Fables|Preface|passage=much less is it in my power to make my commendations '''equal''' to your merits.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} Not [[variable]]; [[equable]]; [[uniform]]; [[even]]. #: Intended for voices of one kind only, either all male or all female; not [[mixed]]. ====Usage notes==== * {{U:en:equal}} * The most common comparative use is the ironic expression {{m|en|more equal}}. * Assertions that all people are equal have never meant that all people are identical or have the same talents, although they are sometimes either miscomprehended or misrepresented as having that
